blocks.text: Optimize your legal transcription workflow
Your day as a legal transcriptionist involves more than just typing. You manage audio files, verify legal citations, and apply strict formatting rules. A slow process here hurts your bottom line.
Start by organizing your workspace. Use Stage Manager or split-screen views to keep your transcription player and your document editor visible. Avoid alt-tabbing if possible.
Mastering legal transcription speed tips for Mac

Speed comes from reducing friction. If you find yourself typing the same phrases repeatedly, use text replacement features in macOS. Go to System Settings > Keyboard > Text Replacements. Create shortcuts for long terms like 'Plaintiff Exhibit Number' or 'Court of Common Pleas'.

When you need to research a specific legal term or verify a spelling, do not switch to a browser manually. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to find the definition or spelling for you. This keeps your focus on the document.
Privacy and compliance in your transcription process

Always follow your employer's rules regarding client data. Do not upload sensitive recordings to cloud-based AI services unless your firm explicitly allows it. Verify if your tools process data locally.
blocks.title: Data Privacy First

blocks.text: Many transcriptionists prefer local tools to ensure attorney-client privilege. When working with sensitive documents, ensure your Mac settings are secure. Check if your transcription software stores audio files in a secure, encrypted folder.
Drafting and editing for high accuracy
AI-generated drafts are common, but human review remains the most critical step. Overlapping speech and thick accents often confuse automated systems. Focus your energy on those difficult segments.

When you need to format your document, you might struggle with complex menus. Ask Lazur to guide you through finding specific features in Microsoft Word or Pages. For example, ask 'How do I add a footnote in Pages?' and Lazur will walk you through the steps.

items: Use custom templates for every case type to save time.
Keep your keyboard shortcuts list on a sticky note near your monitor.
Use a high-quality foot pedal for playback control to keep your hands on the keyboard.
Regularly clean up your desktop to avoid clutter.
Use dictation for notes and quick administrative tasks.

blocks.text: The role of voice in your transcription day

Dictation is a powerful tool when used correctly. Hold the fn key to dictate clean, formatted text directly into your document. This is useful for drafting memos or routine correspondence that does not require playback.
Improving speed with consistent formatting
Formatting errors are a major cause of delays. If you use Microsoft Word, learn the Styles feature. If you use Pages, look at the Format sidebar. Consistency is the key to professional output.

If you are struggling with a specific format, look at our guides on [how to add a footnote in Pages](/how-to/add-a-footnote-in-pages) or [how to see word count in Pages](/how-to/see-word-count-in-pages). These small steps add up to significant time savings.
What to do when you feel stuck
Even experienced transcriptionists hit walls. Maybe you cannot find a setting in Word, or you need to quickly search for a legal citation. Instead of searching menus, use your voice.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask 'Where is the track changes button?' Lazur will circle it on your screen. This is much faster than clicking through multiple submenus.

faq.question: Does Lazur transcribe audio for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant that helps you navigate your Mac, research, and draft text. It does not perform automated transcription of audio files.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur for sensitive legal work?
faq.answer: Lazur processes data only while you hold the shortcut. It does not store your audio or screenshots. However, you must always follow your firm's specific data security and compliance policies.

faq.question: Will Lazur click buttons in my transcription software?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides you by pointing at buttons and explaining steps. You remain in control of your software.
